plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 5: Stereochemistry at Tetrahedral Centers
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic drawing of a polarimeter, laid out as a single optical path running left to right in perspective. At the far left a lit incandescent bulb sits in a socket inside a yellow glow, labeled "Light source", and short red double-headed arrows pointing in many directions emerge from it beneath the label "Unpolarized light". The beam is drawn as a flat pale yellow ribbon that passes through a circular disc with fine vertical striping, labeled "Polarizer", after which the red arrows all lie in a single vertical plane under the label "Polarized light". The ribbon then runs through a horizontal cylinder with a small filling stub on top, drawn with rounded ends and labeled "Sample tube containing organic molecules"; the red arrows inside progressively tip away from vertical as they move along the tube. Beyond the tube the beam meets a second striped disc labeled "Analyzer" and continues to the right, where a heavy red double-headed arrow lies at a slant. A vertical dashed reference line and a curved arrow mark the angle between the two, labeled with the Greek letter alpha, and a drawn eye at the right edge is labeled "Observer". Tracking one ribbon of light through every component makes the tilt of the arrows the quantity to follow. The arrangement shows how the rotation an optically active sample imposes on the plane of polarization is measured.

elements: Light source (incandescent bulb in socket with yellow spherical glow)
Unpolarized light starburst (red double-headed arrows pointing in multiple intersecting planes)
Continuous yellow semi-transparent light beam ribbon tracking along the optical path
Polarizer disc (dark grey outer ring with vertical internal grating)
Polarized light arrow (single vertical red double-headed arrow immediately after polarizer)
Sample tube (semi-transparent grey-blue cylinder with top filling stub)
Progressively twisting red double-headed arrows evenly spaced inside the sample tube
Analyzer disc (dark grey outer ring with internal grating oriented to the analyzer angle)
Outgoing polarized light arrow (red double-headed arrow rotated to the analyzer angle)
Angle measurement overlay: vertical dashed reference line, curved arc, and 'α' label
Observer eye icon at the far right end of the optical path

interactions.label: Sample Optical Activity
interactions.teaches: Determines how much the organic sample twists the plane of polarization as the light propagates through the tube

interactions.label: Analyzer Angle (α)
interactions.teaches: The observer rotates the analyzer disc to align with the incoming light's plane, thereby measuring the sample-imposed rotation α

interactions.label: Send Light Pulse
interactions.teaches: Visualizes the physical flow of light from the source, becoming polarized, twisting in the sample, and passing through the analyzer

demo_steps.title: Inactive Sample
demo_steps.narration: With an inactive sample (0°), light passes straight through without twisting. The analyzer must remain vertical (0°) to let the maximum amount of light through.

demo_steps.title: Optically Active Sample
demo_steps.narration: An active sample rotates the polarization plane by 45°. Because the analyzer is still at 0°, the outgoing light is now misaligned and partially blocked.

demo_steps.title: Measuring Rotation
demo_steps.narration: The observer rotates the analyzer by α=45° to match the new polarization plane. Full brightness is restored, successfully measuring the sample's rotation.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Optical axis lies along the X-axis from -6 to +6. Bulb at X=-5.5. Unpolarized arrows at X=-4.5. Polarizer at X=-3 (RingGeometry radius ~1.2, vertical lines). Polarized arrow at X=-2.5. Sample tube from X=-2 to X=2 (radius ~0.8, cyan-grey #add8e6 opacity 0.25). Inside the tube, array 4 red double-headed arrows along X, their roll angles linearly interpolating from 0 (vertical) to sampleActivity. The yellow beam (#ffcc00, opacity 0.4) is a wide ribbon that physically twists by sampleActivity inside the tube. Analyzer at X=2.5, its grating rotated by analyzerAngle. Outgoing arrow and α overlay at X=3.5, rotated by analyzerAngle. Eye icon at X=5. Red arrows: #e60000.
interactionPlan.notes: To visualize the matching process intuitively (Malus's Law), tie the opacity/brightness of the outgoing beam ribbon and outgoing arrow to cos(sampleActivity - analyzerAngle) so it fades out when misaligned and is solid when matched. The lightPulse animation should slide a brighter localized highlight or a thick packet of arrows along the entire beam path.

authoredContext:
The angle of rotation can be measured with an instrument called a polarimeter, represented in the figure. A solution of optically active organic molecules is placed in a sample tube, plane-polarized light is passed through the tube, and rotation of the polarization plane occurs. The light then goes through a second polarizer called the analyzer. By rotating the analyzer until the light passes through it, we can find the new plane of polarization and can tell to what extent rotation has occurred.

Schematic representation of a polarimeter. Plane-polarized light passes through a solution of optically active molecules, which rotate the plane of polarization.

Schematic representation of a polarimeter. Unpolarized light from light source passes through polarizer, followed by polarized light, sample tube containing organic molecules, analyzer, and observer.

In addition to determining the extent of rotation, we can also find the direction. From the vantage point of the observer looking directly at the analyzer, some optically active molecules rotate polarized light to the left (counterclockwise) and are said to be levorotatory, whereas others rotate polarized light to the right (clockwise) and are said to be dextrorotatory. By convention, rotation to the left is given a minus sign (−) and rotation to the right is given a plus sign (+). (−)-Morphine, for example, is levorotatory, and (+)-sucrose is dextrorotatory.

Demo Steps
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The polarizers and analyzer are disproportionately large relative to the length of the sample tube and overall spacing.
The camera view compresses the setup along the optical axis, causing elements to heavily overlap.
The light beam is rendered as a flat 2D plane rather than a 3D volumetric cylinder or cone.
The labels in the 3D scene are microscopic and completely illegible.
The reference dashed line for the alpha angle is vertical, whereas the original figure uses a horizontal reference line.
evaluation.notes: The underlying physics and interactive elements are excellent, but visual proportions, severe camera foreshortening, and microscopic labels make the visual presentation difficult to parse.
action_items: Adjust the camera azimuth and reduce the radius of the polarizer/analyzer rings to prevent elements from heavily overlapping.
Replace the flat PlaneGeometry light beams with volumetric CylinderGeometry to give them proper 3D substance.
Increase the fontSize of all addLabel calls significantly (e.g., to 24px or larger) so they are comfortably legible.
Change the reference dashed line for the alpha angle to extend horizontally rather than vertically to match the source.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual model and interactivity are excellent, but the execution suffers from implementation details like camera angles, microscopic labels, incorrect object scaling, and using flat planes instead of volumetric cylinders, all of which should be fixed by the generator.
